risk_scan.title: Risk scan
risk_scan.desc: Review the last 24 hours of changes for high-risk issues — runtime errors, data loss, permission bypasses, resource leaks, cross-platform compatibility — with locations and fixes.

release_notes.title: Release notes
release_notes.desc: Collect this week's merged PRs and commits, grouped into features, fixes, UX and engineering improvements, drafting both team and user-facing notes.

nightly_cleanup.title: Nightly code cleanup
nightly_cleanup.desc: Nightly sweep for quality issues — dead code, duplicated logic, stale comments, security risks — fixes are left UNCOMMITTED: the run stops and waits for human review; code is committed only after you confirm.
nightly_cleanup.prompt:
Nightly code cleanup (unattended + human review):
1. Read through the workspace codebase (use git log to spot recent hotspots) and audit against quality standards: dead code and unused exports, duplicated logic, naming/structure issues, overly long functions, missing error handling, leftover TODO/FIXMEs, redundant or misleading comments, obvious security risks (hardcoded secrets, injection, unreleased resources).
2. Only fix "high-confidence + low-risk" issues: keep each change small and revertible, run the project lint/tests after each change, and immediately revert any change that breaks tests.
3. Do NOT run git commit or git push in this round: leave all changes in the working tree, then stop and output a morning report — suggested fixes (file path + what changed + verification result) and items deliberately left alone (with reasons), and wait for human review.
4. A human will review and respond in this session. Only when they explicitly ask you to commit, group the changes into commits by issue type (message explains motivation and scope; still do not push).

mr_review_merge.title: PR/MR review & merge
mr_review_merge.desc: Fully automated review: enumerate open PRs/MRs (or local branches ahead of the baseline), walk through each for correctness, security, test coverage and convention consistency; merge (squash preferred, source branch deleted) only when all merge criteria pass, otherwise reject with file-and-line comments; anything uncertain goes to a human.
mr_review_merge.prompt:
PR/MR review & merge task (unattended; deliverables are review comments and merge/reject decisions):
1. Enumerate pending changes: if GitLab/GitHub MCP tools are enabled (platform Settings → MCP Servers), prefer them to list all open PRs/MRs; otherwise use CLIs (gh / glab) or curl the GitLab/GitHub API on the origin host (/api/v4, works when the repo is anonymously readable); if none are available, fall back to listing local branches and commits ahead of the baseline branch (git log <base>..) and state in the final reply that remote PR/MR lists could not be fetched.
2. Review each one: read the change description and commit split first, then the diff file by file (MCP MR-diff tools or git diff). Focus on: correctness (edge cases, error handling, concurrency, resource release), security (injection, privilege escalation, secret leakage), test coverage (behavior changes must ship tests), and consistency with project conventions.
3. Merge criteria (all must hold before merging): ① scope matches the description and touches nothing off-limits (.gitlab-ci.yml, .github/, CI config, dependency lockfiles, auth or deploy scripts); ② diff size is manageable (≤400 lines recommended, generated artifacts excepted); ③ lint and tests pass locally; ④ no unresolved review comments.
4. Pass → merge (squash preferred, delete the source branch afterwards; GitLab forbids self-approval by the author by default — merge directly, no need to approve first). Fail → leave review comments pinned to files and lines, explicitly listing required changes — never wave it through. Uncertain (cannot verify locally, large cross-module change) → do not merge; mark it as needing human review.
5. Changes with conflicts or missing descriptions are rejected as-is — do not fix them yourself.
6. Final reply: a review ledger — change item → decision (merged/rejected/needs-human) → one-line reason; when auto-merge is unavailable, attach the manual steps (MR/PR link or branch name).
